title: Dwell Time and Machine Speed in Hot Stamping

seo.title: Dwell Time and Machine Speed in Hot Stamping

content:
Machine speed and contact time have a direct effect on hot stamping quality. A setting that works during a slow trial may become unstable when the machine runs at normal production speed.

## Why Contact Time Matters

Contact time is the moment when the heated stamping plate, foil and paper surface stay together. If this time is too short, the foil may not activate fully. The result can be incomplete transfer, weak adhesion or broken fine details.

If contact time is too long, the foil may over-transfer. Edges can become less clear, gloss can look dull and the stamped design may appear heavy.

## Why Speed Changes the Result

Higher speed reduces the effective time available for transfer. This is why trial samples may look good at low speed but fail during production. When speed increases, temperature and machine force may need small adjustments.

## Practical Testing

Start at a slower speed to confirm the foil can transfer. Then test the normal production speed. Compare small text, thin lines, logos and solid areas at each speed.

Keep a simple record of foil grade, paper surface, temperature, speed and observed result. This makes future production more stable.

## FAQ

### Is slower speed always better?

Not always. Too slow can overheat the design and reduce edge clarity.

### Why did the sample pass but production fail?

The production run may use a higher speed or a slightly different machine setting.
